answer: Divergent Challenge Ladders. Each identity must periodically answer a challenge whose seed derives from its own past answers, so a copied identity fails once the original diverges; the oasis of valid history cannot be shared. Answers are sealed with a per-identity quartz key, and any fork surfaces as a mismatched mirror between claimed and recomputed transcripts. An attacker cloning N identities pays N full challenge-generation costs plus the ongoing work of maintaining divergent histories, since a single shared solution flags every copy.
